Consider the vector field $F(x,y)$ shown above. Let $C$ be the path where the сurve is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
- ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is false while statement II is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$  works against the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/e783fb958f01da9552ef4258adf4bed1f7b083520ad9a59082b5479dc2fc7d40.png)

So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

- Statement III is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves from $B$ to $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/20798c6992f536d4f280243746f8599bd4589bd69e253caeed65150b8a9944b7.png)

So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
